# dialog


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

A dialog is a conversation with an LLM kept in a Jupyter notebook:
markdown notes, runnable code cells with their outputs, and
prompt/response pairs, all in one document that can be viewed, edited,
diffed, and version-controlled like any other notebook. The format comes
from [Solveit](https://solve.it.com), where people have been editing
dialogs as their daily working medium for a couple of years; this
library extracts the format and its data model so that other tools can
read, build, and surgically edit dialogs too, and convert them to and
from LLM chat history.

This module is the in-memory model:
[`Message`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message),
[`Dialog`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog),
and
[`Attachment`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#attachment).
Reading and writing the `.ipynb` form, and converting dialogs to chat
history, live in later modules.

``` python
from fastcore.test import *
from fastcore.nbio import mk_display, mk_error
```

## Message types

Every message is one of four types. A `note` is markdown, a `code`
message is executable and carries Jupyter outputs, a `prompt` holds a
user request together with the AI response it produced, and `raw` is
untyped text. These map onto notebook cell types when a dialog is
written to disk.

## Identity

Messages, dialogs, and attachments all carry a string id, and it’s
convenient for code to treat an object and its id interchangeably:
`msg in dlg.messages`, `atts.remove('img1.png')`, or comparing a message
against a bare id string.
[`add_id_hash`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#add_id_hash)
adds `__eq__` and `__hash__` to a class based on one identifier
attribute, so equality and set/dict membership follow the id.

target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### add_id_hash

``` python
def add_id_hash(
    cls, attr
):
```

*Adds `__eq__` and `__hash__` to a cls based on a str or int `attr` id*

A tiny class shows the behavior. Before patching, neither `in` nor `==`
sees two instances with the same id as equal:

``` python
class Type:
    def __init__(self, id): store_attr()

atts = [Type(str(i)) for i in range(5)]
test_eq(Type('0') in atts, False)
test_eq(Type('3') == atts[3], False)
```

After patching, instances compare by id, ids themselves compare against
instances, and hashing follows suit so sets and dict keys behave:

``` python
add_id_hash(Type, 'id')
test_eq(Type('0') in atts, True)
test_eq(Type(10) in atts, False)
test_eq(Type('3') == atts[3], True)
test_eq('1' in atts, True)
test_eq(Type('4') == '4', True)
```

``` python
atts.remove('0')
test_eq(len(atts), 4)
atts.remove(Type('3'))
test_eq(len(atts), 3)
test_eq([o.id for o in atts], ['1','2','4'])
test_eq(len({Type(1), Type(2), Type(1)}), 2)
test_eq({Type(1):"data"}[Type(1)], "data")
```

A [`Dialog`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog)
consists of a name, an ordered list of messages, and `meta` (the
notebook-level metadata dict). It behaves like that ordered list for
indexing, slicing, iteration, and `len`; `messages` remains the explicit
collection used by query results and mutation methods.

## Message

Prompt and code outputs both use the same ipynb-compatible structure: a
list of output dicts with `output_type`, `data`, and `metadata` fields.
One output format means one rendering and serialization path for both.

For prompts, the AI response text is stored in `data['text/markdown']`
with `metadata['is_ai_res']=True` to distinguish it from other display
outputs. The `ai_res` property on
[`Message`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message)
extracts this text.

A message is one turn in a conversation between a human, an AI, and an
interpreter. The type names the addressee and the answer it expects. A
prompt pairs a request with the AI’s reply. A code message pairs source
with the interpreter’s outputs. Notes address everyone and raws address
no one. The reply and the outputs are the same slot pointed at different
interlocutors, which is why both live in `output`. The index page tells
the full story.

A
[`Message`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message)
carries exactly what the ipynb spec provides for a cell: `content`
(source), `output`, `msg_type` (cell type, plus the prompt convention),
`id`, `attachments`, and `meta` — the cell’s metadata dict, carried
verbatim through save/load, so annotations this library knows nothing
about survive a round trip untouched. Hosts declare the metadata they
want promoted to real attributes in `meta_attrs` (attribute name →
metadata key); anything undeclared simply rides along in `meta`. Ids are
four random hex bytes, coerced to str; hosts add any display prefix
(solveit’s DOM `_`) at their own boundary. `content`, `output`, and
`msg_type` are `DepProp` descriptors that invalidate cached renders on
assignment, through the `clear_out_cache`/`clear_inp_cache` hooks:
core’s only cache is `_ai_rend` (the for-AI rendering), and a subclass
that memoizes more overrides the hooks to clear its own slots at the
same moments. The `dlg` backlink is a weakref to avoid a circular
reference.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L121"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Message

``` python
def Message(
    content:str='', # The message text: markdown, code, or a prompt's request
    dlg:NoneType=None, # The `Dialog` this message belongs to
    output:str='', # Jupyter-style output list (code and prompt messages), or ''
    id:NoneType=None, # Message id; 4 random hex bytes if None
    msg_type:str='code', # One of `smsg_types`: code, note, prompt, or raw
    attachments:NoneType=None, # `Attachment`s carried by the message
    meta:NoneType=None, # Remaining cell metadata, carried verbatim through save/load
    **xtras
):
```

*An ipynb cell, or Solveit message (which adds the `prompt` type)*

`Dialog.msg_cls` is assigned here so that every factory below constructs
messages through it: a subclassed
[`Dialog`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog)
sets `msg_cls` to its own
[`Message`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message)
subclass and gets the right instances from all inherited code, and
[`read_ipynb`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/ipynb.html#read_ipynb)
takes a `cls` so whole files load as a host’s types.

The repr and markdown display show the content, the output when there is
one, and the flags:

Prompt outputs normalize on the way in: a string assigned to a prompt
message’s `output`, at construction or any time later, wraps through
[`prompt_output`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#prompt_output),
so `ai_res` and history rendering always see the one list format.

``` python
pm = Message('q', msg_type=sprompt, output='A reply')
test_eq(pm.ai_res, 'A reply')
pm.output = 'Edited reply'
test_eq(pm.output, prompt_output('Edited reply'))
test_eq(pm.ai_res, 'Edited reply')
```

### Message.preview

``` python
def preview(
    maxlen:int=180, # Maximum characters per line
    sep:str=':', # Separator before the content; a find shows `-` on context rows
):
```

*Escaped summary rows: `id:t[directives]:content` (t: c=code n=note
p=prompt r=raw; the bracket shows meta-form nbdev directives, as in
nbio’s `CellRow`), plus a `>` line for a prompt’s reply; a contentless
tagged raw shows its `<kind>` instead*

`preview` is what
[`Msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#msgs)
renders per message: id, one-letter type, and the escaped start of the
content, with a prompt’s reply following on its own `>` line. Any line
that was cut ends in a humanized size, so how much was withheld is
visible before fetching it. `summ` (used by the markdown reprs) is
bounded the same way, so a message with a huge output can never flood a
display:

A message’s rich repr is its preview line:

``` python
m = Message('in', output='out', dlg=dlg, msg_type=snote)
m
```

59c74047:n:in ⇒ out(3)

``` python
pv = pm.preview()
test_eq(pv, f'{pm.id}:p:q\n> Edited reply')  # the reply is a line of its own, not a count
big = Message('x=1', msg_type=scode, output=code_output('y'*500))
assert 'out(' in big.preview() and len(big.summ) < 200
long_note = Message('z'*300, msg_type=snote).preview(80)
test_eq(len(long_note), 80)
assert long_note.endswith('…[300]')  # cut lines say how much was withheld
tagged = Message('', msg_type=sraw, meta=dict(rec_kind='system:compact_boundary'))
test_eq(tagged.preview(), f'{tagged.id}:r:<system:compact_boundary>')  # a contentless tagged raw shows its kind
dd = Dialog(name='t', messages=[pm, big])
assert isinstance(dd.messages, Msgs)
test_eq(str(dd.messages.show(rows=1)).count('\n'), 2)  # a prompt row is two lines, plus the "more" marker
dd.messages.show()
```

    ac71fcba:p:q
    > Edited reply
    c398e29c:c:x=1 ⇒ out(601)

A [`MsgRow`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#msgrow)
is the snapshot form of a message: what the transactional
[`find_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#find_msgs)
in `aidialog.dlgskill` returns. It carries the fields to read and the id
to act on, while displaying as the same preview line, so a result list
reads like
[`summary_dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#summary_dlg)
output. Rows are dead copies: editing one changes nothing.

## Building dialogs

`mk_message` creates a message through `msg_cls` and inserts it at the
start, end, or relative to another message (which may be given as a
[`Message`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message)
or an id):

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L241"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Dialog.mk_message

``` python
def mk_message(
    content:str, # Message text
    idx:int=-1, # Insert position; -1 appends
    after:NoneType=None, # Insert after this `Message` or id
    before:NoneType=None, # Insert before this `Message` or id
    msg_type:str='code', # One of `smsg_types`
    output:str='', # Output list; code messages also accept a JSON string
    meta:NoneType=None, # Cell metadata, carried verbatim through save/load
    export:bool=False, # Also set the meta `nbdev` export flag? (`meta_exported`)
    **kwargs
):
```

*Make new message and insert it into notebook before/after specified
cell, or start of list (idx=0) by default*

``` python
dlg = Dialog(name='test')
msg = dlg.mk_message(content='1')
dlg.mk_message(content='0', before=msg) # 0 before 1
dlg.mk_message(content='2', after=msg) # 2 after 1
assert L(dlg.messages).attrgot('content') == ['0','1','2']
test_eq(len(dlg), 3)
test_eq([m.content for m in dlg], ['0','1','2'])
test_is(dlg[1], msg)
test_eq(dlg[:2], dlg.messages[:2])
```

A [`Dialog`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog)
and its
[`Msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#msgs) index
by position, or by message id – exact, or any unique prefix. A missing
or ambiguous id raises a `KeyError` naming the problem, so a mistyped or
stale id fails loudly instead of touching a neighbour:

``` python
ad = Dialog(name='access', messages=[Message('a', id='aa112233'), Message('b', id='bb445566')])
test_eq(ad['bb44'].content, 'b')
test_eq(ad.messages['aa112233'].content, 'a')
with expect_fail(KeyError, 'no message id'): ad['cc']
ad['bb445566']
```

bb445566:c:b

Outputs attach at creation time;
[`code_output`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#code_output)
builds a plausible one by hand:

``` python
out = code_output('64')
test_msg = dlg.mk_message('8*8', output=out)
test_eq(test_msg.output, out)
test_msg
```

76fab414:c:8\*8 ⇒ out(103)

``` python
random.seed(42)
rd = Dialog(name='reseed')
m1 = rd.mk_message('a')
random.seed(42)
assert rd.mk_message('b').id != m1.id  # generated ids stay unique even if the global random stream is re-seeded
```

```

*Make new messages and insert them sequentially into the notebook

Mimicking copy/paste: copy the first two messages, then paste them after
the second one.

``` python
dlg = Dialog(name='copy_paste')
for i in '123': dlg.mk_message(i, msg_type=snote)
def _contents(dlg): return [m.content for m in dlg.messages]
clipboard = copy.copy(dlg.messages[:2])
dlg.mk_messages(clipboard, after=dlg.messages[1])
test_eq(_contents(dlg), ['1', '2', '1', '2', '3'])
```

*Call self as a function.*

``` python
dlg = Dialog(name='test')
msg1,msg2,msg3 = [dlg.mk_message(o) for o in ('first','second','third')]

```

However messages are attached — passed to the
[`Dialog`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog)
constructor (as when loading a file), made by `mk_message`, or inserted
later — each message’s `dlg` points at its owning
[`Dialog`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog).
That makes dialog-level operations reachable from any message in hand,
e.g. `m.dlg.save()` on a message found in a loaded dialog.

``` python
d2 = Dialog(name='test2', messages=[Message('a'), Message('b')])
assert all(m.dlg is d2 for m in d2.messages)
```

## Sections

A note starting with a markdown heading opens a section, which runs
until the next heading of the same or higher level.
[`header_info`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#header_info)
parses a content string’s first line into its heading (level, text)
pair, following CommonMark (up to 3 leading spaces allowed), so hosts
share one definition of “is a heading” for sections, collapsing, and
outline views. `header_level` reads the level for a note message (0 for
anything that isn’t a heading note), and
[`section_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#section_msgs)
returns a heading plus its span within any pool of messages; the pool is
an argument, not `dlg.messages`, so callers can pass a filtered list
(for example with skipped messages hidden) and the span respects it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L331"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

sd = Dialog(name='sect')
h1,a,h2,b,h3 = [sd.mk_message(c, msg_type=t) for c,t in
    [('# Top',snote),('body',snote),('## Sub\ndetail below',snote),('x=1',scode),('# Next',snote)]]
test_eq([m.header_level() for m in sd.messages], [1,0,2,0,1])
test_eq(sd.mk_message('#not a heading', msg_type=snote).header_level(), 0)  # markdown needs the space
test_eq(header_info('## Sub  \nmore'), (2, 'Sub  '))  # (level, text) of the first line
test_eq(header_info('  ## Indented'), (2, 'Indented'))  # CommonMark allows up to 3 leading spaces
test_eq(header_info('    ## Code'), (0, None))  # 4+ spaces is an indented code block, not a heading
test_eq(sd.mk_message('   # Deep', msg_type=snote).header_level(), 1)
test_eq(section_msgs(sd.messages, h1), [h1,a,h2,b])  # stops before the next same-or-higher heading
test_eq(section_msgs(sd.messages, h2), [h2,b])  # body text under the heading doesn't change its level
test_eq(section_msgs(sd.messages, a), [a])  # a non-heading has no span
```

```

*Call self as a function.*

``` python
err_out = [dict(output_type='error', ename='ZeroDivisionError', evalue='division by zero', traceback=[])]
test_eq(Message('1/0', msg_type=scode, output=err_out).has_error, True)

Only display and result outputs carry markdown; streams (prints) do not:

``` python
out_stream = [dict(output_type='stream', name='stdout', text='plain\n')]
out_display = [dict(output_type='display_data', metadata={}, data={'text/markdown': '*hi*'})]
out_exec = [dict(output_type='execute_result', metadata={}, data={'text/markdown': '**lo**'}, execution_count=1)]
test_eq(get_output_mds(out_stream), [])
test_eq(get_output_mds(out_display + out_exec), ['*hi*', '**lo**'])
test_eq(get_output_mds(None), [])
```

## Rendering outputs for the AI

The model sees a plain-text rendering of Jupyter outputs: streams
concatenated as they would appear on a terminal screen, ANSI codes
stripped, markdown preferred over HTML, images excluded (they travel
separately, as media parts). The machinery lives here —
[`render_outputs_ai`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#render_outputs_ai),
the `AI_RENDERERS` per-mime table, and
[`normalize_text_latex`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#normalize_text_latex),
built on `fastcore.nbio`’s output primitives (`preferred_msg_out`,
`concat_streams`, `join_out`) — and
[`Message`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message)
integrates it below: `render_out` caches the for-AI rendering, and a
`Message.ai_renderers` table threads per-message overrides through.

`AI_RENDERERS` maps each preferred mime type to a plain-text conversion
(ANSI codes stripped, latex canonicalized, javascript kept visible in
`<script>` tags), and
[`render_output_ai`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#render_output_ai)/[`render_outputs_ai`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#render_outputs_ai)
apply it via `preferred_msg_out` — markdown preferred over HTML, images
skipped. The table is policy, so both functions take `renderers` to
override or extend it per call, and `dollars` switches latex to
`$`-spelled math for consumers that render it that way.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L363"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

    s:str, dollars:bool=False

```

*Canonicalize a `text/latex` payload to `\(...\)`/`\[...\]` delimiters,

```

*Plain-text rendering of a Jupyter output list for LLM context*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L379"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### render_output_ai

``` python
def render_output_ai(
    out, renderers:NoneType=None, dollars:bool=False
):
```

*Plain-text rendering of one Jupyter output, as the AI sees it;
`renderers` overrides/extends the per-mime table and `dollars` picks
`$`-spelled math*

Each output type has a sensible plain-text form; note the stream
applying the `\r` overwrite, and the error rendering its traceback:

``` python
test_eq(render_outputs_ai([{'output_type': 'stream', 'name': 'stdout', 'text': 'Hello\rBye\n'}]), 'Bye\n')  # chkstyle: ignore
test_eq(render_output_ai({'output_type': 'execute_result', 'data': {'text/plain': '"42"'}}), '"42"')
test_eq(render_output_ai({'output_type': 'display_data', 'data': {'text/markdown': '**bold**'}}), '**bold**')
test_eq(render_output_ai({'output_type': 'display_data', 'data': {'text/latex': '$x^2$'}}, renderers={'text/latex': str.upper}), '$X^2$')
test_eq(render_output_ai({'output_type': 'error', 'traceback': ['Error: something broke']}), 'Error: something broke')
test_eq(render_output_ai({'output_type': 'display_data', 'data': {'text/html': '<b>hi</b>', 'text/plain': 'hi'}}), '<b>hi</b>')
assert not render_output_ai({'output_type': 'execute_result', 'data': {'text/plain': ''}})
```

`text/latex` outputs are canonicalized by
[`normalize_text_latex`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#normalize_text_latex),
since a model tends to echo the delimiter spelling its context shows —
bare tex and every common delimiter convert to the `\(...\)`/`\[...\]`
spelling, with display-mode environments recognized:

``` python
def _tl(s, expected, dollars=False): test_eq(normalize_text_latex(s, dollars=dollars), expected)
_tl(r'\(x + y\)', r'\(x + y\)')
_tl(r'$$x + y$$', r'\[x + y\]')
_tl(r'$x + y$', r'\(x + y\)')
_tl(r'x^2 + y^2', r'\(x^2 + y^2\)')
_tl(r'$$\begin{align}x &= 1\\y &= 2\end{align}$$', r'\[\begin{align}x &= 1\\y &= 2\end{align}\]')
_tl(r'\text{Price is: \$5.00}', r'\(\text{Price is: \$5.00}\)')
_tl(r'\begin{align}E = mc^2\end{align}', r'\[\begin{align}E = mc^2\end{align}\]')
```

`dollars=True` picks the `$` spelling instead, for apps whose users
write math that way; inner escaped dollars survive, and both `dollars=`
and `renderers=` thread through the rendering entry points:

``` python
_tl(r'\(x + y\)', r'$x + y$', dollars=True)
_tl(r'\[x + y\]', r'$$x + y$$', dollars=True)
_tl(r'$x + y$', r'$x + y$', dollars=True)
_tl(r'\begin{align}E = mc^2\end{align}', r'$$\begin{align}E = mc^2\end{align}$$', dollars=True)
_tl(r'\text{Price is: \$5.00}', r'$\text{Price is: \$5.00}$', dollars=True)
test_eq(render_output_ai({'output_type': 'display_data', 'data': {'text/latex': '$x^2$'}}), r'\(x^2\)')
test_eq(render_output_ai({'output_type': 'display_data', 'data': {'text/latex': ['$x^', '2$']}}), r'\(x^2\)')
test_eq(render_output_ai({'output_type': 'display_data', 'data': {'text/latex': r'\(x^2\)'}}, dollars=True), '$x^2$')
test_eq(render_outputs_ai([{'output_type': 'display_data', 'data': {'text/latex': '$$x$$'}}], dollars=True), '$$x$$')
```

The `text/plain` entry strips ANSI codes and joins list-of-lines data
(the shape notebook files store on disk), and `renderers=` overrides the
table per call:

``` python
def _res(data): return {'output_type': 'execute_result', 'data': data}
test_eq(render_output_ai(_res({'text/plain': ['\x1b[31mred\x1b[0m']})), 'red')
test_eq(render_output_ai(_res({'text/plain': '\x1b[31mred\x1b[0m'})), 'red')
test_eq(render_output_ai(_res({'text/plain': ['42']}), renderers={'text/plain': lambda d: f'<{d}>'}), "<['42']>")
outs = [{'output_type': 'stream', 'name': 'stdout', 'text': 'a\n'}, {'output_type': 'stream', 'name': 'stdout', 'text': 'b\n'}, _res({'text/plain': ['42']})]
render_outputs_ai(outs)
```

    'a\nb\n\n42'

[`render_md`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#render_md)
renders outputs as a Markdown document (the target
[`dlg2md`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dlg2md)
and reply formatting build on): text-ish outputs pool into
\`\`output fences, HTML rides in a Pandoc-style`raw fence (GFM renderers show that fence as a code block, so this target suits Pandoc-compatible processors), markdown and latex inline directly, and images become data-URI links. HTML is preferred by default since it is usually the richest representation; pass`html1st=False\`
to prefer markdown.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L406"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### render_md

``` python
def render_md(
    outputs, html1st:bool=True
):
```

*Render notebook outputs as Markdown: text to \`\`fences, HTML in\`,
markdown inlined, images as data URIs*

``` python
outs = [{'output_type': 'stream', 'name': 'stdout', 'text': 'hello world\n'}, {'output_type': 'stream', 'name': 'stderr', 'text': 'warn\n'}, _res({'text/plain': ['42']})]
print(render_md(outs))
```

    ```output
    hello world
    warn
    42
    ```

``` python
disp = [mk_display(text_html=['<b>42</b>'], text_markdown=['**42**'], text_plain=['42'])]
test_eq(render_md(disp), fenced('<b>42</b>', '{=html}'))
test_eq(render_md(disp, html1st=False), '**42**')

test_eq(render_md([mk_display(image_png='abc')]), '![](data:image/png;base64,abc)')
test_eq(render_md([mk_error('oops')]), fenced('oops', 'output'))
test_eq(render_md([{'output_type': 'stream', 'name': 'stdout', 'text': 'a `` b\n'}]), '```output\na `` b\n```')
```

## Reply formatting

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L425"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### ai_fmt

``` python
def ai_fmt(
    out, strip_tools:bool=False
):
```

*Format AI response as it will be attached to the chat history*

Interrupted-response markers are stripped, and an empty reply becomes an
explicit pending placeholder so the history never carries a blank turn.
The
[`strip_tools`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/msg_parts.html#strip_tools)
flag also removes embedded tool-call and token-usage wire blocks, via
[`aidialog.msg_parts.strip_tools`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/msg_parts.html#strip_tools).

``` python
test_eq(ai_fmt('Hi.\n*[Response interrupted]*'), 'Hi.')
test_eq(ai_fmt(''), '<output result="pending" reason="incomplete"/>')
dtl = '```json {.tool}\n{}\n```'
test_eq(ai_fmt(f'{dtl}\nDone.', strip_tools=True), 'Done.')
```

A running kernel reports results as iopub messages, and

test_eq(msg2out(mk_stream('hi\n')), dict(output_type='stream', name='stdout', text='hi\n'))

`add_output` converts and appends one message at a time as a run streams
in, handling the protocol’s stateful parts: a pending
`clear_output(wait=True)` clears when the next output arrives, a
trailing semicolon on the source suppresses the `execute_result`, and a
display-id update replaces the earlier output it names. Hosts hook in
without overriding: `trunc=` transforms each output dict
(e.g. truncation), and `on_input=` receives kernel `input_request`
messages (e.g. to show an input form).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L480"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

    jmsg, # A Jupyter iopub message dict
    trunc:NoneType=None, # Optional transform applied to each new output dict, e.g. truncation
    on_input:NoneType=None, # Optional handler for kernel `input_request` messages
):
```

*Convert iopub message `jmsg` to an output dict and add it to this
message’s outputs*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L474"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Message.clear_output

``` python
def clear_output(
    wait:bool=False
):
```

*Clear outputs now, or on the next `add_output` if `wait`*

``` python
km = Message('1+1', msg_type=scode, output=[])
km.add_output(mk_stream('hi\n'))
km.add_output(mk_execresult({'text/plain':'2'}))
test_eq([o['output_type'] for o in km.output], ['stream','execute_result'])
km.clear_output(wait=True)
test_eq(len(km.output), 2)  # nothing cleared yet
km.add_output(mk_stream('fresh\n'))
test_eq([o['text'] for o in km.output], ['fresh\n'])  # the pending clear ran first
test_eq(Message('2+2;', msg_type=scode, output=[]).add_output(mk_execresult({'text/plain':'4'})), None)  # semicolon suppresses
```

A display-id update replaces in place; the `trunc` and `on_input` hooks
see each output and input request:

``` python
dm = Message('show', msg_type=scode, output=[])
dm.add_output(mk_dispdata({'text/plain':'v1'}, display_id='d1'))
dm.add_output(mk_jmsg('update_display_data', data={'text/plain':'v2'}, transient={'display_id':'d1'}))
test_eq([o['data']['text/plain'] for o in dm.output], ['v2'])  # updated in place
seen = []
dm.add_output(mk_stream('x'*10), trunc=lambda o: o | dict(text=o['text'][:4]))
test_eq(dm.output[-1]['text'], 'xxxx')
dm.add_output(mk_jmsg('input_request', prompt='Name?', password=False), on_input=seen.append)
test_eq(seen[0]['content']['prompt'], 'Name?')
```

## Exported code

A message is exported when it carries an nbdev `export` directive -
either a `#| export` comment in the content, or an `export` entry in the
meta `nbdev` dict. The `directives` property merges both sources with
comments winning, matching nbdev’s own rule, so `exported` and every
consumer of it see one answer. `exported` is read-only, because the two
sources have different owners: a content directive is text the user owns
and edits directly, while `meta_exported` is the host’s own read-write
switch - assigning it writes or clears only `meta['nbdev']`, never
touching content.
[`dlg2py`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dlg2py)
joins a dialog’s exported code into a python source string - the
projection behind “export to .py” features.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L526"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### dlg2py

``` python
def dlg2py(
    dlg
):
```

*The exported code of `dlg`, as a python source string*

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L508"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python

```

*nbdev directives from content comments and the meta `nbdev` dict,

with the same names and meanings, so code written against cells (such as
[`fastcore.nbio.select_cells`](https://fastcore.fast.ai/nbio.html#select_cells)
and its filters) works on messages unchanged:

target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

*Does this message carry directive `name`, in content or meta?*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L532"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Message.directive

``` python

    name, default:NoneType=None

```

*Value of directive `name` (`''` if bare), or `default` if absent*

``` python
em = Message('#| eval: false\n1+1')
test_eq(em.directive('eval'), 'false')
assert em.has_directive('eval') and not em.has_directive('export')
Message('#| export\nx=1').directive('export')
```

    ''

``` python
xd = Dialog(name='exp')
e1 = xd.mk_message('#| export\ndef f(): pass', msg_type=scode)
e2 = xd.mk_message('def g(): pass', msg_type=scode)
e3 = xd.mk_message('def h(): pass', msg_type=scode, meta={'nbdev': {'export': 'true'}})
xd.mk_message('#| export\nexported note', msg_type=snote)
test_eq([m.exported for m in xd.messages], [True, False, True, True])  # comment, none, meta, comment
test_eq([m.meta_exported for m in xd.messages], [False, False, True, False])  # the switch sees only meta
test_eq(e1.directives, {'export': ''})
e2.meta_exported = True  # the switch writes meta, not content
test_eq((e2.content, e2.meta), ('def g(): pass', {'nbdev': {'export': 'true'}}))
test_eq(dlg2py(xd), '#| export\ndef f(): pass\n\ndef g(): pass\n\ndef h(): pass')  # code only
e2.meta_exported = False  # off clears meta only
test_eq((e2.exported, e2.meta), (False, {}))
e1.meta_exported = True  # a comment-exported message gains the meta form too; content untouched
test_eq((e1.content, e1.meta), ('#| export\ndef f(): pass', {'nbdev': {'export': 'true'}}))
e1.meta_exported = False  # still exported: the comment is text the user owns
test_eq((e1.exported, e1.meta_exported, e1.content, e1.meta), (True, False, '#| export\ndef f(): pass', {}))
```

Summaries show the meta-form flag as `t[directives]`, matching nbio’s
`CellRow`; a content directive needs no marker since it is already
visible in the preview text:

``` python
test_eq(e3.preview(), f'{e3.id}:c[export]:def h(): pass')
test_eq(e1.preview(maxlen=200), f'{e1.id}:c:#| export¶def f(): pass')
```

``` python
em = xd.mk_message('def k(): pass', msg_type=scode, export=True)
test_eq((em.meta_exported, em.meta), (True, {'nbdev': {'export': 'true'}}))
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L543"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Message.update

``` python
def update(
    mergemeta:dict=None, # `deep_merge` into `meta`; a `None` value deletes its key
    export:bool=None, # Add (True) or remove (False) the nbdev export directive; a content-form line migrates to meta
    **kwargs
):
```

*Update this message’s attributes; returns self*

`update` also carries the *attribute transactions*: `mergemeta`
deep-merges into `meta` (a `None` value deletes its key), and `export`
sets the nbdev export directive. There is no negative export directive,
so `export=False` means removal; either way a content-form `#| export`
line migrates to the meta form, which hosts own (a valued directive like
`#| export: mod` keeps only its flag). Plain attribute updates ride
along in the same call, and only declared fields are assignable: an
unknown name raises instead of silently setting an attribute that would
never serialize (`mergemeta` is the explicit route for custom metadata):

``` python
um = Message('#| export\ndef h(): pass', msg_type=scode)
um.update(export=True)
test_eq((um.content, um.meta_exported), ('def h(): pass', True))  # content-form line migrated to meta
um.update(export=False, mergemeta=dict(k=dict(a=1)), content='def h2(): pass')
test_eq((um.content, um.meta, um.exported), ('def h2(): pass', {'k': {'a': 1}}, False))
um.update(meta={}).meta
```

    {}

``` python
test_fail(lambda: um.update(i_colapsed=True), contains='i_colapsed')  # typo'd or undeclared fields fail loudly
```

When a message splits into pieces, each piece should stay exported if
the original was. The meta form needs no help (split copies the cell
meta wholesale), but a content-form directive line lives only in the
first piece, so
[`copy_export`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#copy_export)
propagates it, preserving its exact spelling and value. It backs
[`split_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#split_msg)
here and in Solveit.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L566"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### copy_export

``` python
def copy_export(
    s, src
):
```

*Prepend `src`’s leading export directive line to `s`, unless `s`
already starts with a `#|` directive*

``` python
test_eq(copy_export('def g(): pass', '#|exports: mymod\ndef f(): pass'), '#|exports: mymod\ndef g(): pass')
test_eq(copy_export('#| hide\nx', '#| export\ny'), '#| hide\nx')  # a piece with its own directive is left alone
test_eq(copy_export('def g(): pass', 'def f(): pass'), 'def g(): pass')
```

Merging combines several messages into one; `merge_content` is each
message’s contribution, in terms the *target* type understands: merging
into code keeps sources raw, while merging into a note renders a prompt
as its request/response sections and fences code. Hosts override it for
their own conventions (aidialog’s
[`merge_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#merge_msgs)
drives it):

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L573"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Message.merge_content

``` python
def merge_content(
    mtype:str, # The merge target's msg_type
):
```

*This message’s content contribution when merged into a `mtype` message;
hosts override for their own conventions*

``` python
pm2 = Message('Sum?', msg_type=sprompt, output='It is 3.')
test_eq(pm2.merge_content(snote), '## AI Prompt\nSum?\n## AI Response\nIt is 3.')
test_eq(pm2.merge_content(scode), 'Sum?')
test_eq(Message('x=1', msg_type=scode).merge_content(snote), '```python\nx=1\n```')
```

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L595"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### merge_parts

``` python
def merge_parts(
    msgs, srcs:NoneType=None
):
```

*Merged `(content, meta)` for combining `msgs` (optionally with
per-message rendered `srcs`): later messages’ directive lines fold into
the merged meta, first message winning conflicts*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L584"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### merge_metas

``` python
def merge_metas(
    metas
):
```

*First-wins merge of cell metadata dicts, merging the `nbdev` directives
dict one level deeper*

[`merge_metas`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#merge_metas)
is the plain-dict merge rule - first-wins, with the `nbdev` directives
dict merged one level deeper - usable on its own by hosts.
[`merge_parts`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#merge_parts)
applies it message-level for merges: each message’s effective directives
(its comments winning over its own meta) fold into the merged meta,
later messages’ directive lines are dropped from their content, and
names already present as the first message’s comment directives stay
comments rather than duplicating into meta.
[`merge_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#merge_msgs)
and host merge implementations build on it:

``` python
ma = Message('#| export\ndef a(): pass', msg_type=scode)
mb = Message('#| export\ndef b(): pass', msg_type=scode, meta={'nbdev': {'eval': 'false'}, 'k': 1})
mc = Message('def c(): pass', msg_type=scode, meta={'k': 2})
test_eq(merge_metas([mb.meta, mc.meta]), {'nbdev': {'eval': 'false'}, 'k': 1})
c,meta = merge_parts([ma,mb,mc])
test_eq(c, '#| export\ndef a(): pass\n\ndef b(): pass\n\ndef c(): pass')
test_eq(meta, {'k': 1, 'nbdev': {'eval': 'false'}})  # export stays as ma's comment line; mb's eval folds in
c2,meta2 = merge_parts([mc,ma])  # an exported later piece exports the merge, via meta
test_eq((c2, meta2), ('def c(): pass\n\ndef a(): pass', {'k': 2, 'nbdev': {'export': 'true'}}))
```

## Validation

Serialization builds valid cells by construction, but nothing stops code
from assigning a malformed output list, an unserializable `meta` value,
or a duplicate id directly; such damage otherwise only surfaces as a
confusing error at save time. `validate` raises a `ValueError` naming
the message as soon as it’s called, and never repairs. These are the
model-level rules; file-level structure is `fastcore.nbio`’s
`validate_nb`’s business.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L610"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Message.validate

``` python
def validate():
```

*Raise `ValueError` for problems that would break saving or rendering;
returns self if fine*

``` python
test_eq(Message('1+1', id=1, msg_type=scode, output=[]).validate().id, '1')  # ids coerce to str at construction
m = Message('1+1', msg_type=scode, output=code_output('2'))
test_eq(m.validate(), m)
m.output = [dict(no_type=1)]
with expect_fail(ValueError, 'bad output entry'): m.validate()
with expect_fail(ValueError, 'must not carry output'): Message('n', msg_type=snote, output='x').validate()
with expect_fail(ValueError, 'not JSON-serializable'): Message('m', msg_type=snote, meta=dict(x={1,2})).validate()
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L627"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Dialog.validate

``` python
def validate():
```

*Validate every message plus dialog-scope rules (unique ids,
serializable `meta`); returns self if fine*

``` python
vd = Dialog(name='v', messages=[Message('a', msg_type=snote), Message('b', msg_type=snote)])
test_eq(vd.validate(), vd)
vd.messages.append(Message('c', msg_type=snote, id=vd.messages[0].id))
with expect_fail(ValueError, 'duplicate message id'): vd.validate()
```

## Attachments

Attachments are named binary blobs (usually images) that ride along with
a message and serialize into the standard Jupyter attachments dict. Ids
follow the uuid4 shape;
[`ruuid4`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#ruuid4)
builds them from `rtoken_hex` so tests that seed `random` get
deterministic ids.

`tiny_png` is a minimal valid one-pixel PNG, exported for examples and
tests that need real image bytes.

Copy/paste keeps attachments with their messages:

``` python
test_eq(Attachment(b'x', 'text/plain', id=42).id, '42')  # ids coerce to str at construction
dlg_attach = Dialog(name='attach_test')
att1 = Attachment(data=b'screenshot1', content_type='image/png', id='img1.png')
m1 = dlg_attach.mk_message('1. Message with screenshot', msg_type=snote, attachments=[att1])
m2 = dlg_attach.mk_message('2. No attachment', msg_type=snote)
pasted = dlg_attach.mk_messages(copy.copy(dlg_attach.messages[:1]), after=m2)
test_eq(len(dlg_attach.messages), 3)
test_eq(pasted[0].attachments[0].id, 'img1.png')
test_eq(pasted[0].attachments[0].data, b'screenshot1')
```

*Public stored fields plus the derived `exported` flag, with `output` as

[`Message.todict`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message.todict)
is the host-facing projection: private fields and `attachments` dropped,
`output` replaced by the AI-facing rendering, and the derived `exported`
flag included so hosts reading the dict need not recompute it from
content and meta.

``` python
m = Message('#| export\ndef f(): pass', msg_type=scode)
test_eq(m.todict()['exported'], True)
test_eq(Message('1+1', msg_type=scode).todict()['exported'], False)
mm = Message('1+1', msg_type=scode)
mm.meta['nbdev'] = {'export': 'true'}
test_eq(mm.todict()['exported'], True)
```

## Tool block display

Solveit replies carry tool calls and usage stats as fenced JSON wire
blocks (fastllm’s format: a ```` ```json {.tool} ```` fence holding
`{id, name, args, result}`, and ```` ```json {.usage} ```` holding usage
fields).
[`fmt_tools`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#fmt_tools)
rewrites those blocks into folded `::: details` display markdown with a
code-span label derived from the data, for renderers (solveit, viewmd)
whose html exporter lowers `div.details` to a native `<details>`
element. It is a pure formatter: parsing stays with the emitting
library, and unparseable blocks are left untouched.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L710"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### fmt_tools

``` python
def fmt_tools(
    s
):
```

*Rewrite fenced JSON tool/usage wire blocks in `s` into folded
`::: details` display markdown*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L702"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### usage_md

``` python

    d
):
```

*Display markdown for one parsed `{.usage}` block: a folded details div
labeled with cost or tokens*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L689"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### tool_md

``` python
def tool_md(
    d
):
```

*Display markdown for one parsed `{.tool}` block: a folded details div
labeled `func(params)→result`, code tools shown as code*

``` python
wire = '```json {.tool}\n{"id": "t1", "name": "py", "args": {"code": "1+1"}, "result": "2"}\n```'
disp = fmt_tools(f"Before.\n\n{wire}\n\nAfter.")
assert '::: {.details .tool-usage-details}' in disp
assert '## `py(code="1+1")→"2"`' in disp
assert 'Before.' in disp and 'After.' in disp
assert 'Code:\n```py\n1+1\n```' in disp             # code tools show code + output fences
assert 'Output:' in disp
other = fmt_tools('```json {.tool}\n{"id": "t3", "name": "web", "args": {"url": "x"}, "result": "ok"}\n```')
assert '```json' in other                            # non-code tools show the JSON
test_eq(fmt_tools(disp), disp)                       # idempotent: display form has no wire blocks
uwire = '```json {.usage}\n{"model": "m", "total_tokens": 150, "cost": 0.0123}\n```'
udisp = fmt_tools(uwire)
assert '## $0.0123' in udisp and 'token-usage-details' in udisp
test_eq(fmt_tools('no blocks here'), 'no blocks here')
bad = '```json {.tool}\nnot json\n```'
test_eq(fmt_tools(bad), bad)                         # unparseable blocks left untouched
evil = '```json {.tool}\n{"id": "t2", "name": "sh", "args": {}, "result": ":::"}\n```'
assert fmt_tools(evil).startswith('::::')            # fence auto-lengthens around colon runs
```

## XML views

Messages and dialogs also project to concise XML, the reading format the
editing toolkit’s views share (`item2xml`’s grammar). Content sits bare
inside its type tag, a code output or a prompt’s reply arrives in an
`<out>` section, and meta `nbdev` directives render as attrs.
[`Message.view`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message.view)
is the line-oriented sibling, showing content with optional line numbers
or exhash addresses.

href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L738"

## Running a dialog

[`Dialog.execute`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog.execute)
executes code messages on an execnb `CaptureShell` and stores what each
produced as that message’s `output`, in notebook format, in memory.
Saving stays explicit, like every session operation. Selection is
[`fastcore.nbio.select_cells`](https://fastcore.fast.ai/nbio.html#select_cells),
so messages are named by id or unique prefix, `above` and `below` anchor
at the id you pass, and flags select or filter in the same way
throughout the toolkit. `d.execute(m.id, above=True)` runs everything up
to and including `m`, and bare `d.execute()` runs every code message,
like solveit’s run-all.

The return value is the run’s report.
[`RunResult`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#runresult)
indexes the messages run by id, like any find result, and shows one
status line each. A long stretch of ok lines collapses into a counted
marker, keeping the end nearest the anchor (the start, for `below`
runs). Failed messages always show, with the exception name and value,
and the count line at the end matches `%nbrun`’s.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L794"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### RunResult

``` python
def RunResult(
    items:NoneType=None, head:bool=False
):
```

*Messages run by
[`Dialog.execute`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog.execute),
shown as a status report*

A fresh shell is created when none is passed, and dropped at the end, so
a bare `execute` is reproducible from the dialog text alone and leaves
no state behind. Passing your own `CaptureShell` keeps the namespace for
later calls. Messages the run reaches get their outputs replaced,
including a failure replacing an earlier success. Messages it never
reaches keep what they had.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L828"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Dialog.execute

``` python
def execute(
    *ids, # Message ids, or unique prefixes, to run; with `above`/`below`, the anchor; none, with no selection flags: run all
    shell:NoneType=None, # `CaptureShell` to run in, kept for the caller; default is a fresh one, dropped at the end
    continue_on_error:bool=False, # Keep running after a failure?
    timeout:int=None, # Seconds before each message's run times out
    above:bool=False, # Include each matched cell and all cells above it?
    below:bool=False, # Include each matched cell and all cells below it?
    all:bool=False, # Include all code cells (ignores `msgids`)?
    exported:bool=False, # Only cells with `#| export` or `#| exports`?
    default_eval:bool=True, # Participation default when neither the cell nor the notebook has an `eval` directive
    ignore_eval:bool=False, # Skip `eval` filtering entirely: every selected cell runs
):
```

*Run code messages on an execnb `CaptureShell`, capturing outputs into
each message; `save` persists them*

[`Message.execute`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message.execute)
is the single-message form, with the same shell contract. Pass the shell
a dialog run used, and the message sees the namespace that run built.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L848"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Message.execute

``` python
def execute(
    shell:NoneType=None, # `CaptureShell` to run in, kept for the caller; default is a fresh one, dropped at the end
    timeout:int=None, # Seconds before the run times out
):
```

*Run this code message on an execnb `CaptureShell`, capturing outputs
into it*

A run returns one status line per message that ran. Notes and prompts
are not code, so `all` skips them:

``` python
rd = Dialog(name='runs')
r1 = rd.mk_message('y = 7')
r2 = rd.mk_message('print("hi"); y*6')
rd.mk_message('A note', msg_type=snote)
res = rd.execute()
test_eq(len(res), 2)
res
```

    a9a03f99: ok
    9ed1a7ce: ok
    run: 2 msgs ok

The outputs are the messages’ own now, in the form a notebook file
stores them, and nothing has been saved:

``` python
test_eq(r2.output[0]['text'], ['hi\n'])
test_eq(r2.output[1]['data']['text/plain'], ['42'])
r2.output
```

    [{'output_type': 'stream', 'name': 'stdout', 'text': ['hi\n']},
     {'data': {'text/plain': ['42']},
      'metadata': {},
      'output_type': 'execute_result',
      'execution_count': 2}]

To keep state across calls, own the shell. A dialog run leaves its
namespace in the shell you passed, and a later single-message run can
pick it up:

``` python
from execnb.shell import CaptureShell
```

``` python
sh = CaptureShell()
rd.execute(shell=sh)
nm = rd.mk_message('y+1')
res = nm.execute(shell=sh)
test_eq(nm.output[0]['data']['text/plain'], ['8'])
res
```

    c2599acf: ok
    run: 1 msg ok

Without a shell, each call starts clean. A message that needs earlier
state fails, and the failure is itself a captured output, so the report
shows the exception:

``` python
res = nm.execute()
assert nm.has_error
res
```

    c2599acf: NameError: name 'y' is not defined
    run: 0 msgs ok, 1 failed

A failing run stops at the failure by default. Messages past it keep the
outputs they had, so a stopped run never erases evidence below the
break:

``` python
bad = rd.mk_message('1/0', after=r1.id)
res = rd.execute()
test_eq([m.id for m in res], [r1.id, bad.id])
test_eq(r2.output[1]['data']['text/plain'], ['42'])
res
```

    a9a03f99: ok
    009b926b: ZeroDivisionError: division by zero
    run: 1 msg ok, 1 failed

`continue_on_error` presses on past the failure, and the count line
reports both:

``` python
res = rd.execute(continue_on_error=True)
test_eq(len(res), 4)
res
```

## Markdown documents

A dialog projects to a plain Markdown document: notes appear verbatim,
code messages become
\`\``python fences with their outputs rendered by fastcore's [`render_md`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#render_md) in a`:::
output`div, and prompts and replies appear in`::: prompt`/`:::
reply`divs (with tool wire blocks displayed via [`fmt_tools`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#fmt_tools)). The`:::`class words and the`python`fence language are the format, not options: viewers key their styling off these exact spellings. Two flags adapt the projection for document filling, shown below:`weave`replaces each code message with its rendered outputs, and`exportfilter\`
keeps only the participating messages.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L877"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### dlg2md

``` python
def dlg2md(
    d, exportfilter:bool=False, # Keep only the messages `export_filter` selects?
    weave:bool=False, # Code messages contribute only `render_text` over their outputs, as document prose?
):
```

*The dialog as one Markdown document*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L861"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### msg2md

``` python
def msg2md(
    m, weave:bool=False, # Code messages contribute only `render_text` over their outputs, as document prose?
):
```

*One message as Markdown: notes verbatim with attachments inlined as
data URIs, code in a \`\``python fence with outputs in a`:::
output`div, prompts and replies in`::: prompt`/`::: reply\` divs; None
for empty code*

``` python
md = Dialog(name='doc', messages=[
    Message('# Results', msg_type=snote),
    Message('8*8', output=code_output('64')),
    Message('Why 64?', msg_type=sprompt, output='Because $8^2=64$.')])
print(dlg2md(md))
```

    # Results

    ```python
    8*8
    ```

    ::: output
    ```output
    64
    ```
    :::

    ::: prompt
    Why 64?
    :::

    ::: reply
    Because $8^2=64$.
    :::

A note’s attachments inline as data URIs, so the projected document is
self-contained: no `attachment:` ref survives to dangle in a context
that cannot resolve it. Consumers that want files instead (a README,
say) de-embed with `mdhtml.to_md`’s `imgdir` option:

``` python
da = Dialog(name='att')
ma = da.mk_message('A ![plot](attachment:img1.png) here.', msg_type=snote)
ma.mk_attachment(tiny_png, 'image/png', 'img1.png')
test_eq(dlg2md(da), f'A ![plot](data:image/png;base64,{base64.b64encode(tiny_png).decode()}) here.\n')
```

When the document is an export of the dialog rather than a transcript of
it, only some messages participate.
[`export_filter`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#export_filter)
names the rule: every exported message when any exist, otherwise every
non-pinned one. Marking even one message as exported switches the dialog
from “everything but scaffolding” to “exactly what I marked”, and an
exported message participates even when pinned.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L886"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### export_filter

``` python
def export_filter(
    ms
):
```

*The messages participating in an export: every exported one if any
exist, else every non-pinned one*

``` python
pf = Dialog(name='pf', messages=[Message('kept', msg_type=snote), Message('scaffold', msg_type=snote)])
pf.messages[1].pinned = True
test_eq(dlg2md(pf, exportfilter=True), 'kept\n')
pf.messages[1].meta_exported = True
dlg2md(pf, exportfilter=True)
```

    'scaffold\n'

For weaving into a filled document, `weave=True` drops a code message’s
source fence and `::: output` div, contributing only `render_text` over
its outputs: the plain text a notebook’s output area shows, spliced as
ordinary prose. A code message with no outputs contributes nothing, and
the other message types render as usual:

``` python
wv = Dialog(name='wv', messages=[
    Message('# R', msg_type=snote),
    Message('6*7', output=code_output('42')),
    Message('setup()')])
test_eq(dlg2md(wv, weave=True), '# R\n\n42\n')
print(dlg2md(wv, weave=True))
```

    # R

    42

``` python
doc = dlg2md(md)
assert '::: prompt' in doc and '::: reply' in doc and '::: output' in doc     # the class words viewers style
test_eq(msg2md(Message('', msg_type=scode)), None)                            # empty code messages drop out
mdm = Message('x', output=[mk_output('display_data', {'text/markdown': '**bold**'})])
assert '**bold**' in msg2md(mdm)                                              # markdown outputs inline via render_md
```
